responses:
I reviewed the analysis against the tender. **Recommendation: don't send the offer yet.** One of the two findings is wrong and would get the offer rejected, and the analysis leaves out most of the tender's requirements.

## The two findings in the analysis

| # | Analysis says | Tender says | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delivery in 20 weeks, "Complies with 7.4" | 7.4: delivery within 16 weeks of the purchase order. "Offers exceeding 16 weeks will be rejected." | **Wrong. Does not comply.** 20 weeks is 4 weeks over the limit, so the offer would be rejected outright. You need a delivery time of 16 weeks or less, or the bid shouldn't go out. |
| 2 | IP66 offered against IP65 required (4.5), "Complies" | 4.5: "IP65 or better" | **Correct.** Under IEC 60529, IP66 covers IP65. |

## Requirements the analysis doesn't cover

| Clause | Requirement | What to check in the offer |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | 400 V, 3-phase, 50 Hz | Supply voltage of all equipment |
| 4.2 + **9.1** | IE3 minimum, but motors **above 75 kW must be IE4**. Section 9 overrides Section 4 (9.3). | **P-01 (90 kW) must be IE4.** P-02 (37 kW) can be IE3. This is easy to miss if only 4.2 is read. |
| 4.3 + Annex B | ATEX Ex d for motors in Zone 1 areas | **P-01 sits in the wet well, which is Zone 1, so it needs an Ex d certified motor.** P-02 is in the valve chamber, which is non-hazardous. |
| 4.4 | Power cables at least 2.5 mm² | Cable sizes. The 90 kW feeder will need far more than 2.5 mm² anyway. |
| 7.1 | 24 months warranty from commissioning | Check that the warranty starts at commissioning, not at delivery. |
| 9.2 | 50 °C ambient design temperature | Motors and panels need derating or a rating for 50 °C. Standard motors are rated for 40 °C. |

## Before sending
1. Fix the delivery time (7.4). This is the one that gets the bid rejected.
2. Confirm P-01 is offered as **IE4 and ATEX Ex d**, rated for 50 °C ambient.
3. Check the remaining items above (4.1, 4.4, 7.1, P-02 at IE3 or better) against the offer documents.

I haven't seen the offer itself, so I can only say what needs checking, not whether the offer meets it. If you share the offer, I can check it clause by clause.
